title: Add telemetry decision playbook and token-batch annotator
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Customers and internal SRE runs have shown bursts where token-cost spikes coincide with unusual batching behavior and noisy per-tenant alerts. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a lightweight token-batch annotator that tags invocation-level telemetry with a token_batch_cost_boundary and batch_shape fingerprint, and (2) an operational 'Telemetry Decision Playbook' that codifies alert-to-action decisioning (quiet windows, model fallback, and targeted sampling). Motivation: improve our ability to tie cost/latency anomalies back to batching and kernel contention without increasing high-cardinality telemetry. Changeset overview: - New annotator increments a bounded histogram tag (token_batch_cost_bucket) and attaches a stable batch_shape_id for sampled invocations. - Medium-Hz "slab" sampler service that samples one invocation per short time slab per model/region to maintain visibility while reducing cardinality. - Dashboard: Token Batch Heatmap (medium resolution) showing batch_shape_id vs token_batch_cost_bucket with quick links to sampled traces. - Playbook: runbook that maps common alert signatures to deterministic actions (alert dampening, short quiet-window, model fallback, immediate escalation). - Alert tuning: move per-tenant token-variance alert to a dampened window and add a new heuristic that suppresses noisy tenants using a cost-boundary gate. Checklists: - [x] Implement token-batch annotator (Go) - [x] Add medium-slab sampler (Python) - [x] Dashboard and Grafana panels (JSON) - [x] Playbook and docs (Markdown) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Alert rule adjustments and tests Related: linear ENG-4721 (observability: sampling & playbooks), ENG-4820 (batch-fingerprinting). Notes: this PR is intentionally conservative on cardinality: batch_shape_id is only attached for sampled invocations and cost buckets are coarse (4 fixed buckets). Links: runbook: docs/runbooks/telemetry_decision_playbook.md, dashboard preview: grafana/token_batch_heatmap.json, test harness: telemetry/tests/annotator_test.go

review_comments: Samir: Can we ensure the batch_shape_id is stable across minor model binary updates? Concern is downstream aggregation cardinality. Asked for a brief doc note on stability.

Maya: batch_shape_id is derived from deterministic normalization of the token-length histogram + first N opcodes; added section in telemetry/metrics/README.md describing stability and upgrade considerations.
Leah: e2e looked good but the medium-slab sampler needs a safety cap per-tenant to avoid accidental full sampling under low traffic. Requested a guard.
Maya: added per-tenant cap (max_samples_per_minute) and unit test to enforce it; pushed patch f4d9e3b.
Diego: approved after verifying alerts: decreased false positives on staging by ~62% with playbook enabled; left minor nits on doc formatting.

merge_outcome: Merged into main via squash after approvals from Samir and Diego. No conflicts. Release carried as a telemetry-only change (no customer-facing API changes).
release_notes: Observability: Added token-batch annotator (token_batch_cost_bucket + batch_shape_id), medium-slab sampler to reduce telemetry cardinality, Token Batch Heatmap dashboard, and a new Telemetry Decision Playbook that automates alert damping and remediation guidance. This should reduce noisy alert churn and make cost/latency investigations faster.
additional_context: Operational impact: enabling the playbook on staging reduced alert noise during synthetic cone tests. Performance impact: annotator is path-optimized and measured <0.2ms median overhead on hotpath. Privacy: no new user PII is captured; batch_shape_id is non-reversible.
